target_customer: NATO-aligned militaries, starting with UK units, buying low-cost strike, reconnaissance and training drones
problem: Contested battlefields need cheap, modular, jam-resistant drones; existing systems are expensive and hard to adapt.
business_model: Hardware sales of drones plus swarm control software, to defence customers

founders.name: Alexander Le Maitre
founders.background_notes: Built explosive ordnance disposal training and diagnostic hardware for militaries; self-taught in embedded electronics and PCB design; from Guernsey (YC page).

founders.name: Matthew Le Maitre
education: University of Cambridge, Computer Science (top-ranked graduate per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Began at Cambridge's Mobile Robotics Lab.

technical_complexity.rationale: Hardware, fibre-optic guidance, electronic warfare resilience and autonomy software with a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Many Ukrainian and Western makers sell similar FPV drones; relationships with militaries and certification are the main barriers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A crowded field of small makers per 2026 reporting; no acquisition of Seeing Systems found.

market_need_then: Fibre-optic and low-cost FPV drones reshaped the Ukraine war and drove NATO demand; the company reports collaboration with UK Royal Marines and prototype shipments to Ukraine (self-reported).

identity.visual_style: Console-like site with boot messages and numbered section labels
identity.voice_and_tone: Terse and technical military phrasing, e.g. 'contested theatres'

brand_strength.rationale: Generic company name, though product names are memorable. Banshee also names an unrelated QinetiQ target drone. No press on brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Seeing Systems is an active YC Winter 2026 drone maker riding strong defence demand from the Ukraine war. Two brothers with hardware and Jane Street software backgrounds report UK and NATO interest, but funding and customers are not independently verified, and the low-cost drone field is crowded. No exit reported.
notes: Funding unverified: robotics.press and Nordic9 list $500K attributed to YC; Tectonic Defense says the brothers had not raised outside capital. No round recorded. Team size differs (YC page 7, directories 2). Founding year 2025 per YC, 2024 per robotics.press. Advisory board names appear only on the company site and one secondary site. Competition: no dated sources near 2025 found for named rivals, list left empty.
